theater: 河南道洛陽東境滎陽城

battle.name: 滎陽之戰
battle.theater: 河南道洛陽東境滎陽城
battle.brief: 天寶十四載（755）十二月，安史叛將崔乾祐率精騎攻滎陽，雍丘令張巡與睢陽刺史許遠合兵六千八百人據城死守，焚其木樓、夜襲營寨，斬首千餘級，圍十餘日不能下，終因糧盡退保睢陽。卡面的希臘重步兵從未到過此處：方陣的互相遮蔽，在這座孤城裡換成了城牆、箭雨與共食。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 滎陽之戰是唐與安史叛軍在河南道東部的第一次正面對峙，爆發在天寶十四載（755）十二月。安祿山以范陽三鎮兵起兵、十一月陷落東都洛陽之後，叛軍主將河南尹崔乾祐率精騎與攻城部隊自洛陽東出，指向汴水沿線的州縣。唐廷這時正處在「天子西幸、諸軍待命」的混亂之中：調兵之權在中書省與兵部，邊鎮節度使自募兵、自籌糧，援軍號令屢屢滯留。真正守城的不是禁軍，而是地方團練——雍丘令張巡以鄉兵組成數千眾，睢陽刺史許遠自宋州率兵北上，南陽太守姚誾亦引兵來會，三部合為六千八百人；朝廷的正式編制幾乎沒有增援到場。叛軍方面，崔乾祐以幽州騎兵與河朔降卒為骨幹，攻城靠隨軍工匠臨時造出的木樓、撞車與雲梯，騎兵則用於追逐出城的唐軍，力求速戰速決。河北一線仍留安祿山本人與重兵坐鎮范陽，睢陽方向則由尹子奇接替圍城，十三萬大軍壓境。整個戰區的指揮其實是分裂的：叛軍分兵略地、節節推進，唐廷則靠幾位不肯走的縣令，把汴水糧道一段段釘在原地。
countriesEn: The Battle of Xingyang was the first set-piece clash between the Tang state and the An Lushan rebels in the eastern part of Henan circuit, and it broke out in the twelfth month of the fourteenth year of Tianbao (755). After An Lushan had raised the armies of the three northern commands and seized the eastern capital, Luoyang, in the eleventh month, the rebel commander Henan Yin Cui Qianyou led cavalry and siege troops east out of Luoyang toward the prefectures along the Bian River. The court at that moment was in the disorder of an emperor fled west and armies awaiting orders: the power to move troops lay with the Secretariat and the Ministry of War, the regional military governors recruited and provisioned their own men, and reinforcing columns kept stalling on the road. What actually held the city was not the imperial guard but locally raised militia. Zhang Xun, magistrate of Yongqiu, assembled several thousand village volunteers; Xu Yuan, the governor of Suiyang, marched north from Songzhou with his troops; and Yao Shen, governor of Nanyang, brought his men in as well. Their three contingents together came to 6,800 men, and almost no regular imperial units reached the field. On the rebel side Cui Qianyou's core was cavalry from Youzhou together with surrendered troops from Hebei; his siege train consisted of wooden towers, battering rams and scaling ladders thrown up on the spot by the engineers who marched with him, and his cavalry were used to run down Tang soldiers who sallied out, in the hope of a quick decision. An Lushan himself with a main body still sat at Fanyang in the north, and at Suiyang the siege was taken over by Yin Ziqi with 130,000 men. Command in the whole theatre was in fact split: the rebels dispersed their forces and seized ground step by step, while the Tang state held the Bian supply line in place through a handful of magistrates who refused to leave.
people: 張巡是這場戰役的第一主角。他以雍丘令的身分在亂軍中募兵起義，用鄉間義勇拼出數千人的隊伍，在雍丘一帶拖住叛軍，迫使崔乾祐分兵來攻滎陽。他用兵不靠人數，靠的是城中每一面牆：木樓逼近就射燒它，騎兵挑戰就以長槊與弩矢當場打退，夜襲則派敢死隊燒敵營。韓愈《張中丞傳後敘》記他「每戰不用金鼓，密令出擊，士氣益振」。與他並肩守城的許遠是睢陽刺史，出身世家、沉毅有大將之才，通鑑記兩人「共守孤城，眾寡懸殊」；糧盡之際曾議退兵，張巡不許，寧可與城同存亡。南陽太守姚誾引兵來會，與張巡生死與共，成為睢陽城破時同時殉城的三人之一。叛軍一邊，河南尹崔乾祐以精騎與攻城器械見長；接手睢陽圍城的尹子奇帶十三萬大軍，其先鋒令狐潮驅舟師夜沿汴水逼近城牆，被守軍用夜襲與火攻打退。而唐廷真正能倚靠的大將，是正在河東、河西整軍的郭子儀與李光弼；叛軍那邊決定戰役能拖多久的，是安祿山與史思明。
peopleEn: Zhang Xun is the central figure of this battle. As magistrate of Yongqiu he raised volunteers when the war broke out, assembled several thousand men out of the countryside, and held the rebel advance around Yongqiu, forcing Cui Qianyou to detach part of his force to attack Xingyang. He did not rely on numbers but on every wall of the city: when the wooden towers came up he burned them with fire arrows, when the cavalry challenged he met them on the spot with long spears and crossbow bolts, and at night he sent shock squads to set the enemy camp alight. Han Yu's Postscript on the Biography of Officer Zhang records that he 'never used drums or gongs in battle, gave the order to strike in secret, and the morale of his men only rose'. Holding the city at his side was Xu Yuan, the governor of Suiyang, a man of good family with the steady bearing of a great general; the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance records that the two together 'held a lone city against hopeless odds', and when grain ran short they spoke of withdrawing, but Zhang Xun refused and would rather have shared the fate of the walls. Yao Shen, governor of Nanyang, joined them with his troops and shared the fate of Zhang Xun to the end; the three of them died together when Suiyang fell. On the rebel side, Cui Qianyou was known for his cavalry and his siege equipment, and Yin Ziqi, who took over the siege of Suiyang, brought 130,000 men, his vanguard Linghu Chao driving a boat force up the Bian River by night to the foot of the walls, only to be driven back by a night sally and fire. The great Tang commanders the court could really rely on were Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi, who were meanwhile reorganising their armies in Hedong and Hexi; on the rebel side, the length of the war was in the hands of An Lushan and Shi Siming.
kits: 卡面上是希臘重步兵：圓盾、短矛、青銅頭盔與貼身甲胄，這套裝備在公元前五世紀定型，靠盾牌相接站成方陣，公元前四世紀被馬其頓長槍方陣超越，公元前三世紀又在羅馬與馬其頓的會戰裡屢見其敗；到唐代，希臘方陣早已是博物館裡的東西，滎陽城下沒有一面圓盾。卡面這件兵器放在這場戰役裡，只能當作一面鏡子：希臘重步兵的戰力來自互相遮蔽，唐軍守城靠的是另一種互相遮蔽——城牆、甕城與街壘。雙方真正用過的裝備大致可以排開。攻城一方：木樓，離城數十步即可居高臨下射擊，屢被守軍火箭燒毀；雲梯與撞車，撞車逼近城門時被守軍推出罩著濕布的車把水澆下，濕布吸水增重壓垮器械；還有木鵝這種可水陸移動的攻城塔，以及拋擲飛石與箭雨的機弩。防守一方：方盾與長槊、白羽槊配置在城頭與甕城，專門對付貼城的攻城步兵；床弩與角弓用來壓制城外的木樓與騎兵；矢石、滾木、礫石用來折斷雲梯；把蒿草束在箭上射出去，敵軍以為是勁弩而不敢逼近，稱為蒿矢。馬匹在城下的作用主要是叛軍精騎的衝鋒與追擊；真正決定勝負的裝備其實是糧食——從汴州沿汴水運來的軍糧，一斷，武器再多也沒用。
kitsEn: The card shows a Greek hoplite: a round shield, a short spear, a bronze helmet and a close-fitting corselet, the kit that was fixed in the fifth century BC and fought shoulder to shoulder in a phalanx. It was overtaken by the long pike phalanx of Macedon in the fourth century BC and beaten more than once in the third century BC by Roman and Macedonian battle lines; by the Tang dynasty the Greek phalanx was a museum piece, and not one round shield stood below the walls of Xingyang. The kit on the card can only serve as a mirror here. Greek heavy infantry drew their strength from mutual cover; the Tang soldiers who held a city relied on another kind of mutual cover, walls, barbicans and barricaded streets. The equipment actually used on both sides can be listed. On the attacking side: wooden towers that could stand a few dozen paces from the wall and shoot down at the defenders, burned again and again by fire arrows; scaling ladders and battering rams, and when a ram neared the gate the defenders pushed out a cart draped with wet cloth and soaked it down, the wet cloth taking up the water until its weight crushed the machine; wooden geese that could be moved over land or water as siege towers; and engines hurling stones and showers of arrows. On the defending side: square shields and long spears, including the white-plumed long spear, posted on the walls and in the barbican to meet the infantry that scaled them; heavy crossbows and horn bows used to keep the wooden towers and the cavalry at arm's length; stones, rolling timbers and gravel to break scaling ladders; and arrows made of bound reeds, which the enemy took for strong bowshot and did not dare approach. Horses mattered below the walls chiefly for the rebel cavalry's charge and pursuit. The equipment that really decided the outcome, however, was food: the army grain ferried down the Bian from Bianzhou, and once that line was cut no amount of weapons mattered.
tactics: 滎陽的戰術只有一句話：不與叛軍野戰，死守城池。張巡與許遠進城後先整軍、分區、配給，把六千八百人編在城牆與甕城之後；崔乾祐遣精騎挑戰，許遠出戰擊破之，斬首千餘級；叛軍造木樓逼近，守軍以火箭燒毀，如此反覆數次；張巡又夜遣敢死隊燒敵營，使叛軍不能安心攻城。圍城十餘日不能下，糧盡，兩人商議退保睢陽，張巡斷然不許，最後是形勢所迫才退。轉戰睢陽後防守技術更上一層：修甕城、開地道、以矢石孔分層射擊；敵造雲梯就以滾木礫石折之，敵用撞車就推出罩著濕布的幕車把車壓壞，敵以舟師夜沿汴水偷襲就放火並以鼓噪掩護出擊；每到夜裡，守軍以更鼓與喊聲輪番驚擾敵營，使叛軍屢次自驚潰散。南霽雲自蕭縣借來千餘援兵，途中死傷過半，回到睢陽時將士先食鮮肉再出戰。城破前夜大雪落下，糧盡，張巡殺愛妾以饗將士，與許遠、姚誾、南霽雲慷慨就義。整套戰術的本質，是拿城牆換時間，用士氣與飢餓硬撐對方十三萬大軍的包圍圈。
tacticsEn: The tactics of Xingyang can be summed up in a single line: no pitched battle in the open, hold the city. Once inside, Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan first reorganised the troops, allotted them to sections of the wall and controlled the rations, placing 6,800 men behind the ramparts and the barbican. When Cui Qianyou sent his elite cavalry out to challenge, Xu Yuan went out to meet them and broke them, taking more than a thousand enemy heads; the rebels built wooden towers against the walls and the defenders burned them down with fire arrows, again and again; Zhang Xun also sent shock squads by night to fire the rebel camp, so that the besiegers could never settle down to a siege. After more than ten days the city had not fallen, but grain ran out and the two discussed falling back to Suiyang until Zhang Xun flatly forbade it; in the end it was the logic of the situation that forced the retreat. Once they had fought their way to Suiyang the defensive craft improved still further: barbicans were repaired, tunnels driven under the wall, fire delivered from arrow and stone slits laid on several levels; when the enemy built scaling ladders they were broken with rolling timbers and gravel, when the enemy brought up a battering ram they pushed out a cart draped with wet cloth that drowned the machine under its soaked weight, and when the enemy sent boats up the Bian River by night they answered with fire and with a din of drums covering a sally; every night the garrison beat the watches and shouted in turn, so that the rebel camp was repeatedly thrown into panic and flight. When Nan Jiyun borrowed a thousand men from Xiaoxian, more than half of them were killed on the way, and when they came back to Suiyang the soldiers ate fresh meat before going out to fight. On the night before the city fell heavy snow came down, the grain was gone, Zhang Xun killed the concubine he loved to feed his men, and he, with Xu Yuan, Yao Shen and Nan Jiyun, met their deaths with their heads high. The whole system came down to trading the walls for time, holding out against a besieging army of 130,000 with nothing but morale and hunger.
data: 可核對的數字集中在兵力、年份與距離三處。兵力：滎陽守軍六千八百人，由張巡雍丘之眾、許遠睢陽之兵與姚誾南陽之兵合編，這個數字出自《資治通鑑》與《舊唐書》張巡傳；睢陽最後只剩約一千三百人，張巡收散卒之後仍與將士同食；圍城的叛軍，通鑑記尹子奇大軍十三萬，兩相比較正是以一當十的形勢。斬獲：滎陽首戰破精騎，斬首千餘級；夜襲敵營亦斬數百級。距離與位置：滎陽在洛陽東五十餘里，是東都的門戶；睢陽在宋州（今河南商丘南），距滎陽數百里，沿汴水向東，離叛軍糧道汴州（今河南開封）不過數日水程，張巡據此掐住運糧線。時間：洛陽陷落在天寶十四載十一月，滎陽被圍在同載十二月（公曆755年12月至756年1月），本卡所標的755年12月即指唐人記載的十二月；圍滎陽十餘日不下，糧盡而退；睢陽守至天寶十五載十二月（公曆757年1月），凡十餘月。損耗：城中將士餓死者數千人，舊唐書記三千餘人；南霽雲借來的援兵千餘人，途中死傷過半。年代上，距希臘重步兵定型已過一千二百餘年——這條數字本身就說明卡面兵器與本役無涉。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked fall into three groups: strength, dates and distances. On strength: the garrison at Xingyang numbered 6,800 men, combining Zhang Xun's Yongqiu levy, Xu Yuan's troops from Suiyang and Yao Shen's men from Nanyang, a number taken from the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance and from the biography of Zhang Xun in the Old Book of Tang; by the end at Suiyang only some 1,300 men were left, and Zhang Xun took in stragglers and still ate the same rations as his soldiers. On the rebel side the Mirror gives the army besieging Suiyang as 130,000, and the contrast is the whole point: ten to one. On losses: the opening action at Xingyang broke the rebel cavalry and took more than a thousand heads, and the night raid on the camp took several hundred more. On distances and positions: Xingyang lay a little over fifty li east of Luoyang and was the gateway to the eastern capital; Suiyang stood in Songzhou, south of today's Shangqiu in Henan, several hundred li away and eastward along the Bian, and only a few days of water travel from Bianzhou, today's Kaifeng, where the rebel supply base lay, so by holding Suiyang Zhang Xun had the grain route in his fist. On time: Luoyang fell in the eleventh month of the fourteenth year of Tianbao; Xingyang was besieged in the twelfth month of the same year, which runs from December 755 into January 756, and the December 755 label on this card refers to that Tang twelfth month; the siege of Xingyang lasted more than ten days without success and the defenders withdrew for want of grain; Suiyang was held until the twelfth month of the fifteenth year of Tianbao, January 757, for more than ten months in all. On cost: several thousand of the garrison starved to death inside the walls, the Old Book of Tang recording more than three thousand, and of the thousand reinforcements Nan Jiyun borrowed, more than half died on the road. And one honestly counted figure: the hoplite kit had been fixed more than twelve hundred years before this battle, which says in itself that the weapon on the card had no part in it.
cause: 安史之亂的爆發是這場戰役的遠因。開元天寶年間，唐廷在東北邊鎮大量募兵，把范陽、河東、平盧三鎮交給胡族節度使，天寶十載起又讓安祿山兼領三鎮，兵權與財權盡歸一人；755年（天寶十四載）七月，安祿山以「奉密詔討楊國忠」為名在范陽起兵，蕃漢兵十五萬南下，十月盡取三鎮，十一月陷陳留、鄭州，十二月陷東都洛陽；十二月十三日玄宗奔蜀，留守太子李亨在靈武即位，是為肅宗。洛陽既陷，叛軍下一步就是要打通汴水、泗水一線的漕運命脈，把江淮的糧食運到河北去，而滎陽、雍丘、睢陽正壓在這條線上。直接引爆滎陽之戰的，是崔乾祐的選擇：正面強攻洛陽東面這座距都城五十餘里的城池，既能威懾新附的州縣，又能切斷朝廷從東面調兵的通路。朝廷的反應則暴露了更大的破綻：潼關尚未失守，援軍本可出關，卻在半路逗留不入；郡縣長官或逃或降，只有雍丘令張巡與睢陽刺史許遠願意留在原地，把洛陽以東的防線一寸寸釘住。
causeEn: The outbreak of the An Lushan rebellion is the distant cause of this engagement. Through the Kaiyuan and Tianbao reigns the Tang court recruited heavily on the northeastern frontier and handed the three commands of Fanyang, Hedong and Pinglu to commanders of non-Han origin; from the tenth year of Tianbao it made An Lushan commander of all three, and with them went the power over troops and over money. In the seventh month of the fourteenth year of Tianbao, 755, An Lushan took up arms at Fanyang under the pretext of an imperial order to punish Yang Guozhong, raising a host of Chinese and barbarian troops said to number 150,000. He took the three commands in the tenth month, Gucheng and Zhengzhou in the eleventh, and the eastern capital Luoyang in the twelfth; on the thirteenth the Tang Xuanzong fled west to Shu, and the heir who stayed behind, Li Heng, took the throne at Lingwu as Suzong. With Luoyang taken, the rebels' next step was to open the Bian and Si water routes so that grain from the Jiang-Huai could be carried north to Hebei, and Xingyang, Yongqiu and Suiyang lay squarely across that line. What ignited the Battle of Xingyang directly was Cui Qianyou's choice: to strike this city fifty-odd li east of the capital in force, both to overawe the newly submitted prefectures and to cut the road by which the court could bring troops in from the east. The court's own response exposed a wider flaw. Tong Pass had not yet fallen and reinforcements could have come out of the Guanzhong basin, but the columns stalled on the road; district magistrates fled or surrendered, and only the magistrate of Yongqiu, Zhang Xun, and the governor of Suiyang, Xu Yuan, stayed where they were, nailing the line east of Luoyang down inch by inch.
impact: 滎陽本身沒有守住，但它換來的是時間與名聲。張巡、許遠在滎陽、睢陽兩地以六千八百人拖住叛軍大軍，掩護了唐廷在西部的整軍：郭子儀、李光弼在河東、河西積蓄力量，至德二載（757）九月郭子儀收復長安、十月再取洛陽，叛軍由攻勢轉為守勢，兩京的失而復得與睢陽的堅守在時間上緊緊相接。制度上，這場戰役也把安史之亂的真面目攤開：中央對邊鎮的失控、兩京的淪陷與州縣的望風披靡，同時存在一兩位不肯走的守令，這種對照成為唐人記憶中最刺眼的一筆。張巡、許遠、姚誾死後，唐廷分別追諡忠武、肅、敬，後世立廟配祀，睢陽一城在宋以後被稱為雙忠之地。韓愈元和十七年（802）作《張中丞傳後敘》，專為張巡立傳並駁正睢陽曾降賊的流言；白居易《吊古戰場文》則把張巡、許遠與一般被戰死者並列，讓這場一千二百年前的守城戰進入中國詩文的成敗譜系。政治上，安史之亂自此成為唐朝由盛轉衰的分水嶺，藩鎮割據與宦官專權的格局在此後定型。
impactEn: The city of Xingyang itself was not saved, but it bought time and a name. By fighting at Xingyang and Suiyang with 6,800 men, Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan held the rebel host in place while the court reorganised in the west: Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi built up strength in Hedong and Hexi, Guo Ziyi retook Chang'an in the ninth month of the second year of Zhide (757) and Luoyang in the tenth, and the rebels were driven from the offensive to the defensive. The recapture of the two capitals and the stubborn defence of Suiyang are joined closely in time. Institutionally the campaign also laid the An Lushan rebellion bare: the court's loss of control over the frontier commands, the fall of both capitals, the rush of prefectures to surrender, all set against a couple of magistrates who refused to move, and that contrast became the most cutting line in Tang memory. After Zhang Xun, Xu Yuan and Yao Shen died, the court gave them the posthumous titles Zhongwu, Su and Jing, and later generations built shrines for them, Suiyang being called the place of the twin loyalists from the Song onward. In the seventeenth year of Yuanhe, 802, Han Yu wrote the Postscript on the Biography of Officer Zhang to establish Zhang Xun's record and to refute the rumour that Suiyang had surrendered to the rebels; Bai Juyi's Elegy on the Ancient Battlefield placed Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan alongside the ordinary dead of war, folding a defensive battle from twelve hundred years earlier into the Chinese literary canon of victory and loss. Politically, the An Lushan rebellion became the watershed between the high and the late Tang, and the pattern of regional military governors holding the real power and eunuchs dominating the court was fixed in the years that followed.
result: 結局是悲的：滎陽守不住，糧盡而退保睢陽；睢陽守了十餘月，到天寶十五載十二月（757年1月）大雪之夜，糧盡兵疲，張巡與南霽雲慷慨赴死，許遠、姚誾被俘不屈，睢陽陷落。圍城的叛軍取得了城池，卻沒有取得這支軍隊的戰意——同樣的六千八百人，在滎陽逼退了精騎，在睢陽拖到援軍得以在西北完成部署。回頭看卡面上的希臘重步兵：它一次也沒有踏上滎陽的城頭，甚至在唐代，中華的守城兵早已不用圓盾與短矛。留下來的只有那條原理還活著——方陣之所以結實，靠的是每人替旁邊的人擋住一面盾；睢陽之所以結實，靠的是每人替全城省下一口糧。潼關以東的平原上，終究不是靠個人武勇取勝，而是靠一群人決定不散。
resultEn: The ending was bitter. Xingyang could not be held: with the grain gone the garrison withdrew to Suiyang, and Suiyang was held for more than ten months until the twelfth month of the fifteenth year of Tianbao, January 757, when heavy snow fell on a city empty of food and exhausted of men. Zhang Xun and Nan Jiyun died with their heads high, Xu Yuan and Yao Shen were taken and killed, and the rebels took the walls. Yet they did not take the will of that army: the same 6,800 men had thrown back the elite cavalry at Xingyang and held on at Suiyang long enough for the court to finish deploying in the northwest. Looking back at the Greek hoplite on the card: it never set foot on the ramparts of Xingyang, and by Tang times Chinese defenders had long since abandoned the round shield and the short spear. What survived was the principle behind them. A phalanx is solid because each man shields his neighbour with his shield; Suiyang was solid because each man saved the city a mouthful of grain. On the plains east of Tong Pass the victory was never won by individual valour, but by a body of men who decided not to scatter.
